## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāvedalla Sutta* (MN 43) is an analytical catechism set in Sāvatthī, taking the form of a dialogue between the Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita [Klaus and Hartmann 2007]. Mahākoṭṭhita questions Sāriputta concerning abstruse doctrinal topics, including the mutual inseparability of wisdom (*paññā*), consciousness (*viññāṇa*), feeling (*vedanā*), and perception (*saññā*), which are described as conjoined (*saṃsaṭṭha*) rather than separate mental phenomena [Hung 2010; Nakamura 1980]. The discourse also outlines the five factors supporting right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*) that lead to deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom [Melnikova 2014], the three elements sustaining the living physical body—vitality (*āyu*), heat (*usmā*), and consciousness (*viññāṇa*) [Hung 2010; Hayashi 2013], the limbs of the meditative absorptions (*jhāna*) [Deleanu 2006], and various classifications of mind-deliverance (*cetovimutti*), such as the immeasurable, nothingness, emptiness, and signless liberations [Peoples 2013; Yinshun].

The commentary (*Papañcasūdanī*) describes the dialogue as an inquiry to compare views (*diṭṭhasaṃsandanāpucchā*) and highlights Mahākoṭṭhita's renown for analytical knowledge (*paṭisambhidā*) [Klaus and Hartmann 2007]. Modern scholars note that the text's systematic categorization and definitions of disparate concepts reflect a proto-Abhidharmic stratum of the Suttapiṭaka, representing a transitional development toward scholastic systematization [Analayo 2014; Deleanu 2006]. While the Pali canon pairs this sutta with the *Cūḷavedalla Sutta* under the genre term *vedalla*, northern parallels are instead named after the interlocutors as the *Mahākauṣṭhila-sūtra* [Nyanatusita 2013].

 DharmaNexus confirms these relationships with cross-language alignments to MĀ 211 and the *Upāyikā* (D4094), as well as matches with the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. Comparative studies demonstrate that MĀ 211 places the setting at Rājagaha rather than Sāvatthī, inverts the roles of interrogator and respondent, omits the first absorption limb analysis found in the Pali text, and shares content that the Pali tradition locates in the *Cūḷavedalla Sutta* [Deleanu 2006; Klaus and Hartmann 2007; Yinshun]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies widespread text reuse across 155 texts, most notably with the Citta Saṃyutta (SN 41) regarding deliverances of mind, the Indriya Saṃyutta (SN 48), and later treatises such as the *Visuddhimagga* and *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus].
